scene.requestPrompt: A 1960s Kyoto kissaten with wood paneling, velvet booths, record shelves, siphon coffee, handwritten menu cards, and desserts on small tables.
scene.title: 1960s Kyoto Kissaten Interior
scene.blurb: A cozy, semi-interior kissaten in Kyoto from the 1960s featuring warm wood paneling, intimate velvet booths, a curated record shelf, siphon coffee brewing stations, handwritten menu cards pinned up, and delicate desserts
scene.summary: This diorama recreates a 1960s Kyoto kissaten, an atmospheric tea-and-coffee house, layered with cultural material authenticity. Wood-paneled walls and low velvet booths evoke mid-Showa sophistication, while shelves of vinyl records highlight amiable leisure. Handwritten paper menu cards cluster near the counter bar, reflecting personalized hospitality. The innovative siphon coffee setup anchors a ritual of brewing and serving. Small tables scattered with tiered dessert plates show refined Japanese confectionery culture. Overall, the scene supports detailed zones for brewing, seating, listening, and ordering, ideal for photorealistic architectural editorial photography.

details.title: Velvet Booth Seating
details.body: Plush burgundy velvet booths lined along the dark wood-paneled walls providing cozy seating typical of intimate Kyoto kissaten interiors in the 1960s. The textile shows subtle wear from decades of use, imparting authenticity and warmth.

details.title: Siphon Coffee Brewing Station
details.body: Glass siphon coffee brewers on brass stands, carefully arranged on a polished wood counter with small gas lights underneath, creating a theatrical and precise coffee-making ritual unique to Japanese kissaten culture.

details.title: Handwritten Menu Cards
details.body: Delicately pinned handwritten menu cards on cream-colored paper above the counter. These cards list coffee varieties, tea selections, and cakes in elegant Japanese calligraphy, emphasizing the personalized and artisanal nature of the service.

details.title: Vinyl Record Shelf
details.body: A dark wood wall-mounted shelf filled with 1960s jazz and folk vinyl records, reflecting the musical savant culture of kissaten patrons who often enjoyed listening to records during their visit, contributing to the ambiance.

details.title: Dessert Tables
details.body: Small wooden tables scattered near the booths hold delicate tiered dessert plates containing traditional Japanese sweets such as yokan and castella, demonstrating the cultural integration of Western and Japanese confectionery.

concept.hero: The intimate booth corner with velvet cushions bathed in soft lantern light, adjacent to the siphon coffee bar and hand-lettered menu display.
concept.mood: Nostalgic warmth with a touch of refined leisure and handcrafted care.
concept.layout: Linear arrangement with wood-paneled walls framing booth seating on one side, the siphon coffee counter aligned opposite, and record shelves behind. Small round dessert tables populate the middle semi-open floor. Zones for brewing, serving, and listening form a layered flow.
